task.description:
Investigate GH #482 (ISS-0150, MAJOR): zig build test-integration-svc exits 1 with 63 failing test blocks across 34 files, dominated by PostgreSQL 42P01 'relation tenant_<uuid>.schema_migrations does not exist'. Filed 2026-08-06, verified NOT caused by the ISS-0148/#477 fix (reproduced identically on pre-fix build.zig/clean_test_db.py). Secondary failure modes: C23505 duplicate-key on tenant_<uuid>.process_definitions_pkey, and TC-ISS503-02/03 (GBL-084 LEGACY_RLS removal) assertion failures. A SEPARATE, lower-priority flaky finding (TC-DB-02-04, connection-pool-boundary test, 1-of-3 flake rate) is explicitly noted in the issue as a distinct triage item from the 63 deterministic failures.

ORCH attempted to reproduce with a 180s timeout and the run did not complete in that window (exit 143, timeout) -- this confirms the issue's own scale (34 files) and means your diagnosis pass needs a generous timeout (recommend 600s / 10 minutes minimum) or running scoped subsets of the 34 files first to triage faster.

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce with a proper timeout: `BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test zig build test-integration-svc` (this workspace's DB port is 5453, not the stale shell-inherited 5434 -- always override inline). Capture full output.
2. Root-cause the dominant failure: WHY is a tenant schema reachable (other tables exist / referenced) without its own schema_migrations ledger table having been created? Investigate tenant provisioning code (search for how tenant_<uuid> schemas get created -- likely a migration runner, a provisioning script, or `tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants` related logic) and the migration application logic. Determine: is the ledger table supposed to be created as part of tenant provisioning but a step is missing/broken, or is this a test-setup/fixture problem where tests reference tenant schemas that were never properly provisioned by the test harness itself?
3. Root-cause the secondary C23505 duplicate-key failures and the TC-ISS503-02/03 (GBL-084 LEGACY_RLS removal) failures -- determine if these share the SAME root cause as the dominant ledger-missing issue (e.g. a partially-provisioned tenant schema producing multiple downstream symptoms) or are genuinely separate defects.
4. The TC-DB-02-04 connection-pool flake is explicitly out of scope for the 63-failure fix per the issue's own framing (a separate triage item) -- confirm this assessment and either note it needs its own follow-up issue (check if one already exists) or fold a small, well-justified fix into this run's acceptance criteria #3 ('made deterministic or its sensitivity documented and bounded') if it's genuinely small (e.g. lowering a boundary test value, not touching production pool-sizing logic).
5. Given the scale (34 files, 63 blocks), consider whether this needs to be phased (same batch-cap discipline as GH-495/GH-594/GH-596 earlier this session) -- e.g. if the dominant root cause fix resolves the majority of failures but a handful of files have genuinely distinct, unrelated failure modes requiring separate investigation, split those into a follow-up issue rather than blocking this run on them. Make this call explicitly, don't silently expand scope.
6. Route to CODE-DESIGNER with your full diagnosis. This is very likely to require an actual PRODUCTION CODE fix (tenant provisioning logic), not just a test fix -- the issue's own acceptance criteria explicitly say 'any real production defect found during triage is fixed, not just its test.'
acceptance_criteria: Reproduced with a full run (proper timeout), full failure list captured
Root cause of missing tenant_<uuid>.schema_migrations ledger identified
Secondary failure modes (C23505, TC-ISS503-02/03) assessed for shared vs. separate root cause
TC-DB-02-04 flake explicitly scoped in or out with justification
Phasing decision made explicitly if the fix cannot cover all 34 files in one run
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER, not implemented directly
Assessment of whether this needs a production code fix vs. test-only fix

result.summary:
Third diagnosis pass on GH-482 / ISS-0150. Confirmed (again) that the originally
filed premise -- a missing per-tenant schema_migrations ledger -- is disproven by
design (src/design/iss504_migration_tracking.md): public.schema_migrations
(schema_name, version) is the canonical, single-source-of-truth tracker; stray
per-tenant copies are intentionally dropped by GBL-132. RC-1/2/3 (fixed at PR #519,
2026-08-07) hold: neither original error signature (42P01 tenant schema_migrations,
C23505 process_definitions_pkey) appears anywhere in a fresh full reproduction run.
All 4 previously-forwarded sibling issues (ISS-0182/GH515, ISS-0183/GH516,
ISS-0184/GH517, ISS-0185/GH518) are closed.

Discovered an independent, unmerged branch from the prior day (feature/WF03-GH482-20260808)
that had already re-diagnosed to the same conclusion and progressed to a CODE-DESIGNER
close-out design (src/design/iss0150-gh482-test-integration-svc-closeout.md) mandating
a fresh, workspace-owned database re-measurement before GH-482 can be closed. That
branch stalled at Step 2 and was never merged. This run independently re-executed
that design's fresh-database procedure (source is identical to origin/main -- verified
via git diff, this run's branch carries no source changes).

THE KEY FINDING: the fresh-database re-measurement itself failed at the migration
step, before any test could run. zig build migrate against a genuinely fresh database
fails at migrations/011_webhook_subscriptions.sql with a scope-mismatch guard error
(declaresUnqualifiedTableWork in src/db/migrations.zig). Root-caused to commit a2a8c68
(ISS-0185 / GH#518, merged 2026-08-08) which added '-- scope: public' headers to 9
migration files without qualifying their CREATE TABLE / INSERT INTO statements with
'public.'. Confirmed systemic (not just file 011) by pre-seeding the ledger past 011
and re-running migrate, which hit the identical error at the next affected file
(022_obs06_alerting_state.sql); a full scan found 9 affected files total, all last
touched by a2a8c68. Invisible until now because every long-lived db_test container
(created 2026-08-06, before a2a8c68 merged 2026-08-08) already has these files
ledger-recorded as applied, so migrate silently skips re-evaluating their broken
content -- the exact shared_db_container_trap pattern ISS-0150's own 2026-08-07
resolution documented, recurring against a different migration set.

This is a genuine, currently-live PRODUCTION defect (migrations/*.sql, deployed to
every environment) that breaks fresh-database bootstrap on main, and it is what
currently blocks any trustworthy fresh-database measurement of GH-482's own
acceptance criterion. Filed as ISS-0630 / GH#605 (BLOCKER), registered locally,
queued via tools/queue_add.py, and routed to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 2 of this run) as
this run's actual implementation target.

Secondary findings from the original filing (C23505 duplicate-key, TC-ISS503-02/03
GBL-084 removal) are both confirmed RESOLVED (0 occurrences in current output;
already fixed by the 2026-08-07 RC-1 fix) and do NOT share ISS-0630's root cause.

TC-DB-02-04 (the explicitly-out-of-scope connection-pool-boundary flake) is confirmed
absent from this run and has no prior tracking issue; filed as its own follow-up,
ISS-0631 / GH#606 (MINOR), and queued -- not folded into this run since it is
unrelated and not currently reproducing.

PHASING DECISION: this run does NOT attempt to fix or classify the 35 residual
test-integration-svc failures observed against the shared db_test database. They
cannot be reliably sorted into pre-existing/branch-new/already-covered-by-a-closed-
sibling until ISS-0630 is fixed and a trustworthy fresh-database measurement becomes
possible -- attempting that classification now would repeat the exact
unreliable-shared-database mistake ISS-0150's own resolution already identified.
ISS-0630 (small, well-bounded, single-commit-introduced, 9-file fix) is routed now;
GH-482 / ISS-0150 stays OPEN / PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, explicitly blocked on ISS-0630,
for a follow-up run to re-execute the already-written close-out design once unblocked.
This mirrors the batch-cap discipline used for GH-495 -> ISS-0624/ISS-0625 earlier
this session.

issues.description: ISS-0630 / GH#605: 9 migration files break fresh-database bootstrap (routed to CODE-DESIGNER this run)
ISS-0631 / GH#606: TC-DB-02-04 connection-pool flake, filed as its own follow-up per original issue framing
